item.title: 17 best hotels in Crete with jaw-dropping views we'll be sure to check back into in 2026
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
There are countless reasons why Crete remains one of the most popular Greek Islands. It's big – the largest of the Greek islands, in fact – which means it’s easy to find areas of seclusion and authenticity as well as historical sites and architectural ruins. For active travellers, the gorgeous hiking trails offer plenty of things to do. Those looking to relax will revel in its beaches, which have proper sand, unlike those found on Santorini or Mykonos. Our tip: venture to the eastern side of the island to find sandy stretches that are void of many people at all. Then there’s the food scene and the chance to explore quiet (or rowdy) tavernas where catch-fresh seafood dominates a simple menu of local delicacies. The hotels here seem to get better every year and span everything from romantic boutique boltholes to some of the best family-friendly hotels in Europe. Villas too, are a popular choice for multigenerational groups looking to soak up the surroundings in the comfort of a private space. Here, we round up the best hotels in Crete, tried and tested by our editors. Editor's picks of the best hotels in Crete: What is the best location to stay in Crete? Crete is the biggest island in Greece and home to some of our favourite Greek island hotels. Those visiting for the first time are spoilt for choice on where to stay. The obvious choice is Chania in the northwest, where hotels such as Domes Zeen Chania cascade down the hillside and overlook the sea, making it the ideal spot to settle for a week soaking up the Cretan sun. But the eastern half of the island is also well worth exploring. Near-deserted beaches and some of the best Airbnbs in Crete spell escapism; go now before it becomes better known. What's the best resort in Crete for families Direct flights from London make Crete a popular choice for families, and the island is home to some of the best family-friendly hotels in Greece, so booking a multigenerational trip is easily done. Domes of Elounda overlooks the UNESCO-protected island of Spinalonga. Book into self-catering facilities that offer the perfect set-up for families with little ones. When is the best time to visit Crete? Traditionally aligned with a European summer, the hottest months in Crete are between June and September. Many hotels close during the winter. Those visiting during shoulder season – April, early May and October – will be rewarded with quieter beaches, a slower pace, and a sense of locality. This is when the tourists disperse and the spotlight is on Crete’s verdant grounds, fresh food and sublime sea. Every hotel on this list has been selected independently by our editors and written by a Condé Nast Traveller journalist who knows the destination and has stayed at that property. When choosing hotels, our editors consider both luxury properties and boutique and lesser-known boltholes that offer an authentic and insider experience of a destination. We’re always looking for beautiful design, a great location and warm service – as well as serious sustainability credentials. We update this list regularly as new hotels open and existing ones evolve. Find out more about our editorial standards and how we review hotels. This is our edit of the best hotels in Crete. item.title: Pinnacle Studio 26 Ultimate takes on Premiere Pro with a one-time fee
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News
Adobe Premiere is one of the biggest names in video editing, but at $240 for the year, it doesn't make sense for every creator. Pinnacle Studio 26 Ultimate is our favorite subscription-free alternative. Pay once, and it's yours forever (you can even pay a reduced rate to upgrade to the next edition, but that's definitely not essential). Right now, Pinnacle Studio 26 Ultimate is down to $90 (was $130) - and in the UK, it's priced at £80 (was £115). If you don't need complex multi-cam editing or masking tools, the more basic Studio 26 is $40 (was $60), or £40 (was £60). • Best for: Windows users who want advanced video editing features without an ongoing subscription. • What we like: Unlike lightweight video editing apps, it supports 4K video editing across unlimited tracks and multi-camera editing for footage captured from up to six cameras. Other features include motion tracking, video masking, green screen effects, and advanced color grading. • What to know: Pinnacle's video editing software is Windows-only, and lacks the support for plugins that you get from Premiere Pro and Resolve. This advanced video editor features unlimited tracks, six-camera multicam editing, full color grading, motion tracking, smart object tracking, video masking, blend modes, 360-degree editing, and alpha channel export capabilities. This video editor offers six editing tracks, two-camera multicam editing, simplified color grading, keyframe effects, motion controls, a title editor, screen recording, and video capture for creating polished video projects. Adobe Premiere Pro is an excellent choice for professional editors, but not everyone needs everything it offers. Pinnacle Studio 26 Ultimate is a much more affordable alternative with plenty of tools to explore. We rated it the best subscription-free video editing software in our guide. In our review the previous edition, Studio 25 Ultimate, we found it "offers professional post-production polish without subscription costs." Minor niggles with the slow import section aside, we found it ticked all the boxes for general video editing workflows that don't need the pro-grade output of Pro and DaVinci Resolve. On top of the features we've discussed, you can use masking to hide distracting objects, blur sensitive information, or apply effects to selected areas of a scene. The software also includes keyframe controls, letting you adjust the position, size, speed, and appearance of elements throughout your video. For audio, there's voiceover recording, noise reduction, and audio ducking, which automatically lowers background audio to make narration easier to hear. Pinnacle Studio 26 Ultimate is currently priced at $89.99, a $40 saving from the regular price of $129.99. In the UK, it's £79.99, down from £114.99. Unlike Adobe Premiere's subscription model, this is a one-off payment, which is great if you only do a spot of video editing when needed. Adobe Premiere costs $22.99 a month on an annual plan billed monthly, or $263.88 if you pay for the year upfront. Alternatively, you can pay $34.49 a month without an annual commitment. In all, that means a single year of Adobe Premiere could cost you more than three times the price of Pinnacle Studio 26 Ultimate. If Pinnacle Studio 26 Ultimate seems a bit on the expensive side, you can always buy the standard version of Pinnacle Studio 26 for $39.99, down from $59.99. In the UK, it's £39.99, down from £59.99. Should you buy it? ✅ Buy Pinnacle Studio 26 if... You want a Windows video editor with advanced features but don't want to keep paying for an Adobe subscription. It's particularly appealing if you regularly create YouTube content, tutorials, travel videos, or personal projects and want more control than basic editing software provides. ❌ Skip Pinnacle Studio 26 if... You already rely on Adobe Premiere for professional projects, especially if you use other Adobe applications or need to exchange projects with collaborators. It's unsuitable if you use a Mac, as Studio 26 is designed for Windows.
